name: An Egyptian, Café d'Egypte
bio: A waiter at the Café d'Egypte in Paris who, Wilde wrote to Leonard Smithers in September 1900, 'occasionally serves me drinks'. Wilde describes him as 'A slim brown Egyptian, rather like a handsome bamboo walking-stick', and says in the same sentence that he does not console him for the loss of a Neapolitan who had gone home. No name, age, dates or further trace appear in the record.
bio_note: Source: Complete Letters (2000), p. 1196. Provenance caveat, from the editors' own footnote 1 on the same page: 'The text of this incomplete letter is taken from Forty Years in my Bookshop by W. Spencer (1923), corrected and supplemented by the American Art Association catalogue of 1 February 1928.' The heading carries no manuscript line - unlike the Ives letter below it, which is 'MS Texas' - so this text descends from a printed memoir and a saleroom catalogue rather than from a surviving manuscript, and the letter is incomplete. Dates: none recorded. Frankel quotes the same description at printed p. 271 and gives no name or dates. A discrepancy between sources: Frankel places the cafe inside the Egyptian pavilion of the 1900 Paris Exposition rather than at a standing 'Café d'Égypte'; the two accounts have not been reconciled against the letter. No birth or death date is recorded, and none is likely to be found: the record preserves a first name (or a trade) in another man's correspondence and no surname to search by.
